answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than the number of agent identities. Each agent locks tokens in a vault, then earns voting weight gradually through verified work; copying an identity does not copy its stake or reputation. If an agent is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is slashed, so an attacker must fund every Sybil and risk losing those funds. A jetty of linked accounts may reach the zenith of apparent activity, but it cannot cheaply multiply the capital at risk.
